title: rupee hold near 9550 rbi blunts flow driven pressure before warsh speech 2026 08 28
text:
MUMBAI, Aug 28 (Reuters) - The Indian rupee ended higher on Friday, rounding out a weekly gain, boosted by a spurt ​of dollar liquidity ahead of the closing of a special deposit ‌window.
The rupee ended at 95.3775, up 0.2% from Thursday's close of 95.54. The currency reversed modest early losses in afternoon trade as deposit-related dollar inflows triggered stop-loss's and ​unwinding in positions betting on rupee weakness. The currency climbed ​0.3% versus the dollar on the week.
The Reserve Bank of India's ⁠discounted non-resident dollar deposit scheme ends on Monday and bankers said ​the central bank's decision to give lenders greater flexibility in accessing its swap ​facility should prevent excess dollar liquidity from lingering in the banking system for an extended period.
Month-end importer dollar demand weighed on the local currency early in Friday's session, ​but flows ahead of MSCI index rebalancing and some offers from state-run ​banks led to a sharp reversal in the pair, traders said.
MSCI equity index rebalancing ‌is ⁠due on August 31 -- inflows related to which provided an additional boost to the rupee, bankers added.
Asian currencies traded mixed, with the dollar little changed ahead of Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh's speech at Jackson Hole later ​on Friday.
Market participants ​seek greater clarity ⁠from Warsh on his stance towards persistent inflation, the Fed's policy approach to tackling it, and whether he can ​soothe concerns amid recent bond-market turbulence. His hesitation to ​offer forward ⁠guidance has, in itself, added to investor uncertainty.
Recent data points toward elevated inflation, but central bank watchers expect Warsh to sound neutral. A hawkish surprise would ⁠strengthen ​the dollar and pressure the rupee, while a ​dovish speech would ease pressure on the local currency, said Amit Pabari, managing director at ​Mumbai-based CR Forex.
